rows.title: Timing Belt Premature Wear and Failure
rows.howToFix: Inspect the timing belt system immediately if there is any chirping, ticking, front-engine noise, or unknown service history, and verify belt condition by removing the upper timing cover to check for cracking, fraying, oil contamination, slack, and pulley wobble. Repair requires a complete timing belt service: replace the timing belt, hydraulic/mechanical tensioner, idler pulleys, and strongly consider the water pump, front cam/crank seals, and accessory belts at the same time; on these interference engines, do not continue driving if belt timing is suspect. If the belt has already jumped or broken, perform a compression or leak-down test and inspect for bent valves before installing new parts, as cylinder head repair may be required. Typical preventive timing belt service runs about $500-$900 depending on parts replaced, while a failure with valve damage can raise repairs to roughly $1,500-$3,000+.
